questions.question: Which animal has a long trunk?
questions.explanation: An elephant uses its trunk to smell, drink, pick things up and even to hug other elephants.

questions.question: What is a baby cow called?
questions.explanation: Baby elephants, giraffes and whales are also called calves.

questions.question: Which animal has a very long neck and spots?
questions.explanation: A giraffe's neck is so long that it can eat leaves high up in the trees.

questions.question: What do giant pandas mainly eat?
questions.explanation: A panda can eat bamboo for many hours every day.

questions.question: Which animal carries its baby in a pouch and hops?
questions.explanation: A baby kangaroo is called a joey. It lives in its mother's pouch for months.

questions.question: What is a baby bear called?
questions.explanation: Bear cubs are born very small and stay with their mother for a year or more.

questions.question: Which black-and-white striped animal lives in Africa?
questions.explanation: Every zebra has its own pattern of stripes, just like people have fingerprints.

questions.question: Which big cat has a mane?
questions.explanation: Male lions grow a mane, which makes them look big and strong. Lions live in groups called prides.

questions.question: Which mammal can fly?
questions.explanation: Bats are the only mammals that can truly fly. Flying squirrels can only glide from tree to tree.

questions.question: What do we call animals that eat only plants?
questions.explanation: Cows, deer and rabbits are herbivores. Animals that eat meat are called carnivores.

questions.question: What covers the back of a hedgehog?
questions.explanation: A hedgehog rolls into a ball when it is scared, so only its spines show.

questions.question: Which animal builds dams in rivers?
questions.explanation: Beavers cut down trees with their strong teeth and build dams and lodges with the wood.

questions.question: Which white bear lives near the North Pole?
questions.explanation: Polar bears hunt on the sea ice and have thick fur to stay warm.

questions.question: What do mother mammals feed to their babies?
questions.explanation: Giving milk is one thing that all mammals have in common.

questions.question: Which animal gives us wool?
questions.explanation: Most sheep have their wool cut once a year. This is called shearing.

questions.question: What is a baby horse called?
questions.explanation: A young female horse is called a filly, and a young male is called a colt.

questions.question: Which desert animal has one or two humps?
questions.explanation: A camel's hump stores fat, not water. The fat gives it energy on long walks.

questions.question: Which small red-brown animal with a bushy tail climbs trees in Danish forests?
questions.explanation: Red squirrels hide nuts and seeds in autumn and find them again in winter.

questions.question: What do we call a group of wolves?
questions.explanation: A wolf pack is like a family. It usually has parents and their young.

questions.question: Which large animal beats its chest with its hands?
questions.explanation: Gorillas beat their chests to show how strong they are. They eat mostly leaves and fruit.

questions.question: Which slow animal sleeps in trees and hangs from branches?
questions.explanation: Sloths eat and sleep while hanging upside down. They are good swimmers too.

questions.question: Which Australian animal eats eucalyptus leaves?
questions.explanation: Koalas get most of their water from the leaves they eat.

questions.question: Which wild animal is the ancestor of the dog?
questions.explanation: Dogs were first tamed from wolves many thousands of years ago.

questions.question: What do cows eat?
questions.explanation: A cow spends many hours a day eating grass and chewing it.

questions.question: Which animal has no teeth and catches insects with its long sticky tongue?
questions.explanation: Anteaters eat ants and termites. A giant anteater can flick its tongue in and out up to 150 times a minute.

questions.question: Which animal grows antlers on its head?
questions.explanation: Antlers fall off every year and new ones grow back.

questions.question: Which animal sprays a smelly liquid to scare enemies?
questions.explanation: A skunk gives a warning first. It stamps its feet and lifts its tail.

questions.question: Which animal has a horn on its nose?
questions.explanation: Some kinds of rhino have one horn, and others have two.

questions.question: Which animal has long ears, hops and lives in a burrow?
questions.explanation: Wild rabbits live in groups and dig networks of tunnels called warrens.

questions.question: Which pet purrs when it is happy?
questions.explanation: A cat can also purr when it is hurt or scared. Purring may help it feel calm.

questions.question: Which small animal digs tunnels underground and has tiny eyes?
questions.explanation: Moles dig with their big front paws. They find worms with smell and touch.

questions.question: What do all mammals have on their bodies?
questions.explanation: Even whales have a few hairs, at least when they are young. Hair helps most mammals stay warm.

questions.question: Which animal is a horse's cousin with long ears?
questions.explanation: Donkeys are strong and calm. People have used them to carry loads for thousands of years.

questions.question: Which animal pulls Father Christmas's sleigh in stories?
questions.explanation: Real reindeer live in the cold far north. Their thick fur keeps them warm in the snow.

questions.question: What is a baby sheep called?
questions.explanation: Lambs are often born in spring. Their mother is called a ewe.

questions.question: Monkeys, apes and humans all belong to which group?
questions.explanation: Primates have hands that can grip, and big brains for their size.

questions.question: Which striped big cat lives in the jungles of Asia?
questions.explanation: Tigers like water and are strong swimmers. Many other cats keep away from water.

questions.question: Which wild animal is the ancestor of the farm pig?
questions.explanation: Wild boars live in forests. They dig in the soil with their snouts to find food.

questions.question: Which animal has a black-and-white striped face and lives in a sett?
questions.explanation: Badgers dig large underground homes called setts, and come out at night.

questions.question: Which small pet stores food in its cheeks?
questions.explanation: A hamster's cheeks can stretch to carry seeds back to its nest.

questions.question: Which Australian mammal lays eggs?
questions.explanation: The platypus and the echidna are the only mammals that lay eggs. The babies still drink milk.

questions.question: How do bats find insects in the dark?
questions.explanation: Bats are not blind, but in the dark they make high calls and listen to the echoes. This is called echolocation.

questions.question: Which animals follow the rains in a huge yearly journey across the Serengeti?
questions.explanation: Over a million wildebeest travel in herds. Many zebras travel with them.

questions.question: Which ape lives in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra?
questions.explanation: Gorillas and chimpanzees live in Africa. Orangutans live only in Asia.

questions.question: Which mammal is covered in scales that protect it?
questions.explanation: A pangolin curls into a ball when it is in danger. It eats ants and termites.

questions.question: About how long is an elephant pregnant before the calf is born?
questions.explanation: This is longer than any other land mammal. A newborn calf weighs about 100 kilograms.

questions.question: Which Australian animal has fingerprints almost like human ones?
questions.explanation: Koalas' fingerprints are so like ours that they are hard to tell apart under a microscope.

questions.question: How many neck bones does a giraffe have?
questions.explanation: Humans have seven neck bones too. A giraffe's are just very, very long.

questions.question: Which marsupial lives in the Americas rather than Australia?
questions.explanation: The Virginia opossum carries its babies in a pouch. When scared, it may pretend to be dead.

questions.question: Which relative of the giraffe has zebra-like stripes on its legs?
questions.explanation: The okapi lives in the rainforests of Central Africa. Scientists first described it in 1901.

questions.question: Which water-loving South American rodent is as big as a large dog?
questions.explanation: Capybaras live in groups near rivers and swim very well.

questions.question: What do meerkats take turns doing while the group looks for food?
questions.explanation: The guard stands tall and barks if it sees a hawk or a snake.

questions.question: What colour is a polar bear's skin under its white fur?
questions.explanation: The dark skin may help it soak up the sun's warmth. Each hair is see-through and only looks white.

questions.question: Which wild cat with tufted ears lives in the forests of Norway and Sweden?
questions.explanation: The lynx hunts alone, mostly at night. It is shy and hard to see.

questions.question: Which Nordic deer is special because both males and females grow antlers?
questions.explanation: In most other deer, only the males have antlers.

questions.question: What can grow in a sloth's fur that helps it hide in the trees?
questions.explanation: The green colour helps the sloth blend in with the leaves.

questions.question: What is special about the front teeth of rodents like mice and beavers?
questions.explanation: Rodents gnaw on hard things such as wood and nuts to wear their teeth down.

questions.question: Which sense is the strongest in a dog?
questions.explanation: A dog's nose can pick up smells that people cannot notice at all.

questions.question: What do cats use their whiskers for?
questions.explanation: Whiskers help a cat feel the shape of small spaces, even in the dark.

questions.question: Which animal can sleep standing up by locking its leg joints?
questions.explanation: Standing lets a horse run from danger quickly, but it must lie down for deep sleep.

questions.question: What may a zebra's stripes help to keep away?
questions.explanation: Studies show that flies find it harder to land on striped coats.

questions.question: Which ape uses sticks to catch termites?
questions.explanation: Chimpanzees push a thin stick into a termite mound and pull it out covered in insects.

questions.question: Which African animal makes a sound like laughing?
questions.explanation: The hyena's giggle is a way of talking to others in its clan, not a sign of fun.

questions.question: Which big cat has claws that do not fully pull back into its paws?
questions.explanation: The cheetah's claws work like running spikes and give it grip.

questions.question: Which spotted cat of the Asian mountains has a long, thick tail?
questions.explanation: It uses its tail for balance and wraps it round its body like a scarf to keep warm.

questions.question: Which small deer, called rådyr in Danish, is common in Denmark?
questions.explanation: Roe deer are shy and are often seen at the edge of fields at dawn and dusk.

questions.question: Which of these animals is a rodent?
questions.explanation: Hedgehogs look similar but are not rodents. Porcupines are related to mice and beavers.

questions.question: What colour is a giraffe's tongue?
questions.explanation: The dark colour may protect the tongue from the sun while it eats.

questions.question: What is a group of kangaroos called?
questions.explanation: A mob can have a few kangaroos or more than a hundred.

questions.question: How many stomach chambers does a cow have?
questions.explanation: A cow chews its food, swallows it, brings it back up and chews it again.

questions.question: Which African animal has a name meaning "earth pig" in Afrikaans?
questions.explanation: The aardvark digs for ants and termites at night with its strong claws.

questions.question: How many humps does a Bactrian camel have?
questions.explanation: The one-humped camel is called a dromedary. Bactrian camels live in Central Asia.

questions.question: What is the name of Australia's wild dog?
questions.explanation: Dingoes probably came to Australia with seafarers thousands of years ago.

questions.question: Which small animal is famous for fighting snakes such as cobras?
questions.explanation: A mongoose is very fast and can dodge a snake's strike.

questions.question: What does "nocturnal" mean for an animal?
questions.explanation: Bats, owls and hedgehogs are nocturnal. They sleep by day.

questions.question: Which large wild cattle species lives in the forests of Poland and nearby countries?
questions.explanation: The European bison, or wisent, almost died out. Wisents were saved by breeding in zoos and then set free in forests.

questions.question: Which shaggy animal of Greenland's tundra forms a ring to protect its calves?
questions.explanation: Adults stand shoulder to shoulder with their horns out when wolves come near.

questions.question: Why do pigs roll in mud?
questions.explanation: Pigs cannot sweat much. Mud cools their skin and protects it from the sun.

questions.question: Which monkey has a bright blue and red face?
questions.explanation: The male mandrill's colours become brighter when he is excited.

questions.question: In a lion pride, which lions do most of the hunting?
questions.explanation: The lionesses often hunt together as a team. The males mainly defend the pride's land.

questions.question: What is the name for egg-laying mammals like the platypus and echidna?
questions.explanation: The name means 'one hole' in Greek. Their young hatch from leathery eggs and then drink milk.

questions.question: How many tiny bones are in a mammal's middle ear?
questions.explanation: They are the hammer, anvil and stirrup. Reptiles have only one bone there.

questions.question: What forms most of a bat's wing?
questions.explanation: Bats belong to the group Chiroptera, which means hand-wing in Greek. Their long finger bones hold the skin out like an umbrella.

questions.question: Which member of the hyena family feeds mainly on termites?
questions.explanation: The aardwolf can eat hundreds of thousands of termites in one night.

questions.question: Which animal makes cube-shaped droppings?
questions.explanation: Wombats leave their droppings on rocks and logs to mark their territory. The cube shape may stop them rolling away.

questions.question: Which kind of teeth are an elephant's tusks?
questions.explanation: Tusks are upper front teeth that keep growing all through the elephant's life. Warthog tusks, by contrast, are canines.

questions.question: What is a rhino's horn made of?
questions.explanation: Keratin is the same material that forms hair and fingernails.

questions.question: Which animal family does the giant panda belong to?
questions.explanation: DNA studies show that the giant panda is a true bear, even though it eats mostly bamboo.

questions.question: Which small rock-dwelling animal is a distant cousin of the elephant?
questions.explanation: Hyraxes look like guinea pigs, but their feet and teeth show they are related to elephants.

questions.question: Why do koalas sleep for most of the day?
questions.correct: Their leaf diet gives little energy
wrong: They stay awake all night to hunt
questions.explanation: Eucalyptus leaves are hard to digest and low in energy, so koalas save it by resting.

questions.question: Which small African mammal lives underground in a colony with one queen?
questions.explanation: Naked mole-rats live like ants or bees, with workers and one queen who has the babies.

questions.question: What kind of sound do elephants use to talk over long distances?
questions.explanation: Much of the rumble is too low for people to hear. It travels through the air and the ground for kilometres.

questions.question: Which wild ancestor of farm cattle died out in Europe in the 1600s?
questions.explanation: The aurochs was bigger than most modern cattle. The last one died in a royal forest in Poland in 1627.

questions.question: Which horse of the Mongolian steppe vanished from the wild and was brought back from zoos?
questions.explanation: It is named after the explorer Nikolai Przhevalsky. In Mongolia it is called takhi.

questions.question: How many toes does a horse have on each foot?
questions.explanation: A horse's hoof is really one big toenail. Its ancestors had several toes.

questions.question: Which of these animals are the closest relatives of horses?
questions.explanation: Horses, rhinos and tapirs are all odd-toed hoofed animals.

questions.question: Which northern forest animal in the weasel family is also called a glutton?
questions.explanation: The wolverine is strong and can eat leftovers of large animals, even frozen meat.

questions.question: Which small forest rodent sleeps through most of the winter and has golden-brown fur?
questions.explanation: The hazel dormouse sleeps for about half of the year and builds a nest of grass and leaves.

questions.question: Which land mammal lived in Iceland before people arrived?
questions.explanation: The Arctic fox probably came over the sea ice. The other land mammals that live there, such as mice and reindeer, were brought by people.

questions.question: Which small Nordic animal is known for its mass migrations?
questions.explanation: Lemmings do not jump off cliffs on purpose. An old nature film helped to spread that myth.

questions.question: What do reindeer dig through the snow to find in winter?
questions.explanation: Reindeer have wide hooves that work like snowshoes and help them dig.

questions.question: Which male mammal has a venomous spur on its back leg?
questions.explanation: The venom is strong enough to cause great pain in people. It is used in fights with other males.

questions.question: Why do cats' eyes shine in the dark?
questions.correct: A mirror layer behind the retina
questions.explanation: The mirror layer sends light back through the eye, which helps cats see in dim light.

questions.question: Which colours do dogs see best?
questions.explanation: Dogs see fewer colours than people do, but they are not colour-blind.

questions.question: Besides their fur, where else do tigers have stripes?
questions.explanation: If you shaved a tiger, you would still see its stripes.

questions.question: Which South American animal is the wild ancestor of the llama?
questions.explanation: The alpaca came from the vicuña. Guanacos and vicuñas live wild in South America.

questions.question: What is the offspring of a male donkey and a female horse called?
questions.explanation: A hinny has a horse father and a donkey mother. Mules are strong and good at carrying loads.

questions.question: Which tiny fox of the Sahara has huge ears that help it lose heat?
questions.explanation: The fennec's big ears also help it hear insects moving under the sand.

questions.question: What are deer antlers made of?
questions.explanation: Antlers grow fast and are covered in soft velvet until they are fully grown.

questions.question: Which striped marsupial from Tasmania died out in the 1930s?
questions.explanation: It was also called the Tasmanian tiger, but it was not related to tigers.

questions.question: Which small mammal feels for food with 22 fleshy tentacles on its nose?
questions.explanation: It lives in wet ground in North America. Its nose has thousands of tiny touch sensors.

questions.question: The giant panda's "thumb" is really an enlarged what?
questions.explanation: The extra bone helps the panda hold bamboo stems like a hand.

questions.question: Which bear is the only one native to South America?
questions.explanation: It has pale rings around its eyes that look like glasses.

questions.question: Which armoured animal of the Americas usually has identical quadruplets?
questions.explanation: All four babies come from one egg, so they are identical.

questions.question: What is a scientist who studies mammals called?
questions.explanation: Ornithologists study birds, entomologists study insects and herpetologists study reptiles.

questions.question: What does the name "orangutan" mean in Malay?
questions.explanation: Orang means person and hutan means forest.

questions.question: Which farm animal descends from the wild mouflon?
questions.explanation: Mouflons are wild sheep that live on islands and in mountains of Europe and Asia.

questions.question: Why are beavers' front teeth orange?
questions.explanation: The iron makes the enamel harder, so the teeth stay sharp on wood.

questions.question: Which lemur taps tree trunks to find insect grubs?
questions.explanation: It listens to the taps and then gnaws a hole and pulls out the grubs with a long thin finger.

questions.question: What are a giraffe's horn-like bumps called?
questions.explanation: Ossicones are bone covered with skin and fur. Both male and female giraffes have them.
